issue: Two correct answers: distractor (a) 'Management's excessive interest in maintaining the stock price' is itself an attitude/rationalization risk factor listed in the standards, yet it is marked wrong and its rationale says it 'leans toward incentive or pressure'. The item is used on aud-mock-1 and aud-mock-3.
evidence: AU-C 240 Appendix A and AS 2401.85 (Risk factors for fraudulent financial reporting, Attitudes/Rationalizations) list 'Excessive interest by management in maintaining or increasing the entity's stock price or earnings trend' next to 'recurring attempts by management to justify marginal or inappropriate accounting'. The AUASB copy of the same ISA-based appendix (standards.auasb.gov.au/node/2056) lists it under attitudes/rationalisations. The incentive/pressure version in the appendix is different: 'significant portions of compensation contingent on achieving aggressive targets for stock price'. A candidate who knows the appendix picks (a) and is scored wrong. Blind answer (b) matched the key but flagged (a) as also correct.
source: AU-C 240 Appendix A (Attitudes/Rationalizations); PCAOB AS 2401.85; https://standards.auasb.gov.au/node/2056
fix: Replace (a) with a genuine incentive/pressure factor, e.g., 'A large part of management's bonus depends on meeting an aggressive earnings target' (explanation: 'That is an incentive or pressure: compensation contingent on aggressive targets'). Alternatively keep the stock-price wording and make it the key, removing (b). Keep trap 'wrong-classification'.

issue: Ambiguous classification, and it contradicts the lesson. The stem's 'repeatedly overrides policies' reads as opportunity. The lesson's fraud-triangle diagram lists 'override' under Opportunity, and AU-C 240.A1 ties opportunity to a belief that controls can be overridden. But the key is Attitude and the explanation for (b) rejects Opportunity.
evidence: Lesson line 56: 'O[Opportunity: weak controls, override, complex transactions]'. AU-C 240.A1: opportunity exists when an individual believes internal control can be overridden. AU-C 240 App. A (misappropriation, attitudes): 'disregard for internal control over misappropriation of assets by overriding existing controls'. Both readings are supported, so a student following the lesson picks (b).
fix: Remove the override wording and use an unambiguous attitude factor from App. A, e.g., 'Management repeatedly fails to remedy known significant deficiencies on a timely basis and dismisses misstatements as immaterial.' Rewrite (b)'s explanation to say that the ability to override controls is the opportunity, while a disregard for controls is the attitude. Add that distinction in one line under the lesson diagram.

issue: The rule for communicating to those charged with governance is incomplete. The lesson body (line 106), the 'Communicate' key takeaway and the aud-fr-04 item explanation say TCWG hear of 'fraud involving senior management, or fraud causing a material misstatement'. AU-C 240.40 also covers fraud involving any member of management and employees with significant roles in internal control, whatever the amount. It also requires the auditor, when management fraud is suspected, to discuss with TCWG the nature, timing and extent of the procedures needed.
evidence: AU-C 240.40: 'if the auditor has identified or suspects fraud involving (a) management, (b) employees who have significant roles in internal control, or (c) others, when the fraud results in a material misstatement ... the auditor should communicate these matters to those charged with governance on a timely basis.' The platform's own aud-written-representations lesson (line 62) and aud-tbs-r3-rep-letter use the 'management, employees with significant roles in internal control, or others where material' formulation, so the platform states the rule two ways. The lesson's wording is AS 2401.79 (PCAOB), but the lesson cites both standards. An exam item about immaterial fraud by an employee with a key control role would be missed.
fix: Lesson line 106 and the takeaway: 'to those charged with governance: fraud involving management or employees with significant roles in internal control (any amount), and other fraud that causes a material misstatement; if management fraud is suspected, also discuss the procedures needed (AU-C 240.40). PCAOB AS 2401.79: senior management, or any fraud causing material misstatement, goes to the audit committee.' Update aud-fr-04's overall explanation to match.

issue: Skill labels are two levels too high, and difficulty is inflated. Four straightforward communication-rule items are labelled evaluation, and a pure recall item (aud-fr-20) is labelled analysis. All but aud-x2-20 are difficulty 3, although their distractors are 'do nothing', 'report publicly' or 'only …' options.
evidence: aud-fr-13 (CEO fraud → tell TCWG), aud-fr-26 (immaterial clerk theft → inform management), aud-fr-27 (CFO fraud → TCWG) and aud-x2-20 (mid-level fraud → evaluate implications, tell management) each apply one stated rule to one fact. That is Application, not Evaluation. aud-fr-20 ('which period should JE testing cover?') recalls AU-C 240.32(a)(ii)-(iii) and is Remembering, not Analysis. In this module, practice and exam items show evaluation 5/33 and difficulty 3 on 11/27 practice items. Those mislabels feed the Blueprint skill-mix and readiness weighting.
fix: Relabel aud-fr-13, -26 and -27 as application, difficulty 1–2. Relabel aud-x2-20 as application, difficulty 2. Relabel aud-fr-20 as remembering, difficulty 1. To keep evaluation coverage for objective 3, write one or two genuine evaluation items, e.g., a scenario in which management refuses to act on CFO fraud: evaluate the effect on reliance on representations and whether to withdraw (AU-C 240.36, .38).

issue: Skill or difficulty labels are one level off.
evidence: aud-fr-05 (evaluation) applies the TCWG rule: application or analysis. aud-fr-15 (analysis, d3) is an obvious 'obtain support' response: application, d2. aud-fr-17 (application) asks why a retrospective review is done: remembering. aud-fr-18 (analysis, d3) recalls AU-C 240.32(c): application, d2. aud-fr-19 (analysis, d3) resolves inconsistent responses: application, d2. The TBS (analysis) classifies 6 given facts into triangle elements and fraud types and recalls the required procedures, which is application. 20 minutes for 16 dropdown cells is also generous.
fix: aud-fr-05 → analysis. aud-fr-15 → application, d2. aud-fr-17 → remembering. aud-fr-18 → application, d2. aud-fr-19 → application, d2. TBS → application, about 15 minutes, or add a genuine analysis part (e.g., link each risk to the account and assertion and choose a response).

issue: Redundancy: 'which procedure is required to respond to management override?' is asked four times in nearly the same form. aud-fr-12 is essentially a copy of the inline check aud-fr-chk2, with the same key and the same receivables, inventory or cash and payroll distractors. The TBS 'resp' part and flashcard f3 drill the same list again.
evidence: cues.md Jaccard: chk2~12 0.56, chk2~23 0.56, 12~23 0.50. Keys: chk2 (a) retrospective review; 12 (a) retrospective review; 23 (d) testing journal entries; x2-19 (b) testing journal entries. Distractor families repeat: confirm receivables or cash, observe inventory or count cash, payroll.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (same fact >3 times)
fix: Keep chk2 and x2-19. Rewrite aud-fr-12 to test another facet, e.g., that the retrospective review is not meant to second-guess the prior year's judgments, or which estimates it covers (significant ones). Rewrite aud-fr-23 to test the overall responses (AU-C 240.29: assignment of personnel, evaluating accounting-policy choices, unpredictability), or what still applies when the revenue presumption is rebutted.

issue: Near-duplicate pairs. The aud-mock-2 exam item aud-x2-31 repeats the lesson pre-question aud-fr-pre1, so the mock tests memory of a seen item. The practice items aud-fr-04 and aud-fr-26 are the same scenario with the same key.
evidence: pre1: 'which fraud risk does the auditor presume exists in every audit, with no way to rebut it?' Key: management override; (a) improper revenue recognition. x2-31: 'which fraud risk is presumed in every audit and cannot be rebutted?' Same key, same (a). aud-fr-04: immaterial $2,000 inventory theft by a warehouse clerk → appropriate level of management, with an SEC distractor. aud-fr-26: immaterial theft by a junior clerk → 'inform suitable management', with an SEC distractor.
fix: Rewrite aud-x2-31 as a scenario, e.g., a single fixed-rent revenue stream where the revenue presumption is rebutted: which fraud-related procedures are still required, and what must be documented? Rewrite aud-fr-26 to test a different communication case, e.g., immaterial fraud by the payables supervisor who approves vendor master-file changes (a significant control role, so TCWG; ties to the AU-C 240.40 fix).

issue: Answer cues. In aud-fr-12, aud-fr-18 and aud-fr-20, every distractor carries an absolute ('all', 'only', 'nothing') and the key is the only qualified option. In aud-fr-05, aud-fr-27 and aud-x2-20, only the key combines two actions ('…; …'), so it is the visibly 'most complete' option. aud-fr-02's key is 33% longer than any other option.
evidence: aud-fr-12: b 'Confirming all receivables', c 'Observing all inventory counts', d 'Testing all controls over payroll'. aud-fr-20: a/b/c all start 'Only…', d 'Period-end and the full year'. aud-fr-18: a 'Only the cash…', c 'Only its legal form', d 'Nothing, if…'. Compound keys: 05 'Tell those charged with governance; reassess management's representations', 27 'Reassess risks; tell TCWG', x2-20 'Its implications…; tell management'. aud-fr-02 option lengths a52/b43/c38/d69 characters.
fix: Remove the absolutes or put one in the key too (e.g., aud-fr-20 distractors: 'Period-end entries only, because fraud is concentrated there'; 'Entries above performance materiality'). Give one or two distractors a compound form as well (e.g., 'Tell the CEO; obtain an additional written representation'). Shorten aud-fr-02 (d) to 'One person dominates management unchecked' or lengthen a distractor.

issue: Implausible distractors make difficulty-3 items trivial. Options such as 'Ignore it', 'Ignore both', 'Report it publicly', 'To the press', 'Report the fraud directly to the police', 'Accept it because the CFO has authority' and 'Defer testing to next year' model no real misconception. In aud-fr-27, (a) 'Treat it as immaterial' and (c) 'No action is needed at all' are the same idea.
evidence: Each listed item has at least one distractor no candidate would choose. aud-fr-13 (a, c, d), aud-fr-15 (a, b), aud-fr-19 (d), aud-fr-26 (a), aud-fr-27 (a, c), aud-fr-08 (b) and aud-x2-20 (d). Effectively 2-option items.
fix: Use real exam misconceptions. Communicate only to the level of management above the perpetrator. Communicate to TCWG only if material. Obtain an additional written representation instead. Withdraw immediately. Extend substantive tests without communicating. Report to the SEC under Section 10A (wrong because the conditions aren't met). For aud-fr-19: accept internal audit's answer because internal audit is independent of management.

issue: Trap labels don't fit. 'partial-computation' is used for non-numeric 'incomplete answer' distractors, and in aud-fr-05 (a) the error is a wrong rule (the wrong level of communication), not a partial answer.
evidence: partial-computation on: aud-fr-03 b ('Nothing further'), aud-fr-05 a ('only to the CFO, who oversees the CEO's staff': the CFO is subordinate to the CEO, and AU-C 240 requires at least one level above, i.e., TCWG for the CEO), aud-fr-09 b, aud-fr-10 a, aud-fr-18 a and c, aud-fr-20 a, b and c. None involves a computation.
fix: Use 'wrong-rule' for aud-fr-03 b and aud-fr-05 a, and 'overgeneralization' or 'other' for the rest. Or add an 'incomplete' trap type to the schema. Also reword aud-fr-05 (a) to a plausible error: 'Communicate only to the CFO and the controller, who are not involved'.

issue: Thin or mismatched explanations that don't teach the rule.
evidence: aud-fr-06 key: 'Correct. Several risk characteristics.' (doesn't name them). aud-fr-17 key: 'It's a required fraud procedure.' (doesn't say how bias shows: comparing prior estimates with outcomes). aud-fr-17 (c): 'Not related to these facts.' (the stem has no facts). aud-fr-18 key: 'It may signal fraudulent reporting.' aud-fr-22 a/b/d: 'That is not the model.' ×3. aud-fr-23 a/b/c: 'Not override-specific.' ×3. aud-fr-24 b/c/d: 'The data don't indicate that.' ×3 (should explain that a 45→80-day DSO jump with flat-industry 40% growth points to receivables that are not collecting, i.e., existence and occurrence; understated expenses or excess inventory would show in margins or inventory turnover).
fix: Rewrite each key explanation to state the rule (e.g., aud-fr-06: 'Period-end, a senior user who doesn't normally post, a round amount, no description, revenue account: AU-C 240.A49 characteristics'). Give each distractor its specific reason.

issue: The explanation for distractor (d) 'Report it to the SEC at once' reads 'Not the first step.' That implies an immaterial clerk theft is later reported to the SEC. Nothing says the client is an issuer, and outside disclosure is barred except for legal or regulatory requirements, subpoenas, successor auditors and funding agencies.
evidence: Lesson line 108 and AU-C 240.42 / AS 2401.82: confidentiality generally precludes outside reporting. Section 10A reporting requires an illegal act with a material effect that management and the board fail to remediate.
fix: Change to: 'No outside reporting is required. Immaterial employee theft is communicated to an appropriate level of management, and confidentiality bars disclosure to regulators unless law, a subpoena or a similar exception applies.'

issue: The explanation for (c) says 'The predecessor is not the required source.' Since SAS 147 (AU-C 210, periods beginning on or after June 30, 2023), a successor auditor must ask the predecessor about identified or suspected fraud, once management authorizes it. The distractor is still wrong as a whole, but its rationale states the rule too broadly.
evidence: review/reference/aud-standards.md §2: SAS 147, Inquiries of the Predecessor Auditor Regarding Fraud and NOCLAR. The successor must inquire about identified or suspected fraud (verified). The AU-C 240 inquiry set (management, TCWG, internal audit, others within the entity) is separate, and legal counsel is not a required fraud-inquiry source.
source: AU-C 210 as amended by SAS 147; AU-C 240.17–.21
fix: (c) explanation: 'AU-C 240's required inquiries are of parties within the entity. In an initial audit, AU-C 210 (SAS 147) separately requires asking the predecessor about known or suspected fraud, but legal counsel is not a required source.'

issue: The overall explanation cites 'AU-C 240.39' for communicating senior-management fraud to TCWG. Paragraph .39 is the communication to the appropriate level of management. TCWG communication is .40.
evidence: AU-C 240.39: identified fraud or information that fraud may exist → appropriate level of management. AU-C 240.40: fraud involving management, employees with significant roles in internal control, or others where material → those charged with governance. Numbering is from memory and the search did not return the paragraph text.
fix: Change the citation to AU-C 240.40 (and .38 for considering withdrawal).

issue: The lesson is thin for a heavily tested topic. Several items test content the lesson never teaches, and several AU-C 240 requirements are absent.
evidence: The triangle diagram gives only 2–3 examples per element, and there is no Appendix A risk-factor table split between FFR and misappropriation. Items test factors not in the lesson. Domination by one person or ineffective board oversight: aud-fr-02, TBS f2. Disregard for controls: aud-fr-11 b, aud-fr-16. Stock-price interest and 'industry practice': aud-x2-18. Living beyond means: aud-fr-14. Inconsistent inquiry responses → corroborate (AU-C 240.20): aud-fr-19. Unpredictability examples appear only in a takeaway: aud-fr-07. Absent from the lesson altogether: the overall response of evaluating the selection and application of accounting policies (AU-C 240.29b); skepticism specifics (.12–.14: records may not be genuine; inconsistent responses); evaluating audit evidence (late-stage analytics, .34; whether a misstatement indicates fraud and what that implies, .35–.36); documentation (.43–.46). Inquiries appear only in a takeaway. 505 body words + 399 frontmatter words for 17 minutes.
fix: Add a compact risk-factor table (3 elements × FFR/misappropriation, 3–4 App. A examples each, including domination by one person, failure to remedy known deficiencies, excessive interest in stock price, lifestyle beyond means). Add short body sections on skepticism and inquiries, overall responses (including accounting-policy evaluation), evaluating evidence, and documentation. Add an inline check on attitude vs. opportunity.

issue: Tests lapping (with kiting and channel stuffing as distractors), but this lesson never defines these schemes. Lapping is taught later, in aud-revenue-receivables (AUD-III, unit u7), and is mentioned only in passing in aud-internal-control. The item is also difficulty 3 and analysis.
evidence: grep: 'Lapping: stealing a customer's payment and covering it with a later customer's payment' appears only in content/aud/modules/aud-revenue-receivables/lesson.md:35. aud-internal-control/lesson.md:89 mentions it only in an insight. The aud-fraud-risk lesson has no mention of lapping, kiting or channel stuffing.
fix: Add a 'common schemes' row to the lesson's two-kinds table (lapping, kiting, channel stuffing, bill-and-hold, ghost employees, fictitious vendors), or move aud-fr-25 to aud-revenue-receivables.

issue: Research part: excerpts (a) and (b) have the same citation 'AU-C 240 (paraphrase)', and the results screen shows the citation as the answer. A learner who picks (b) sees '✗ … You: AU-C 240 (paraphrase) · Answer: AU-C 240 (paraphrase)'. Section-level citations also don't practise the paragraph-level citation the real research task requires.
evidence: src/lib/tbsScoring.ts research case: given = given?.citation, expected = ex?.citation. src/components/TbsView.tsx:128 renders 'You: {given} · Answer: {expected}'. Excerpts a and b both carry citation 'AU-C 240 (paraphrase)'.
fix: Cite paragraphs: a = 'AU-C 240.26 (paraphrase)', b = 'AU-C 240.32 (paraphrase)', c and d with their paragraph numbers. Or have the results screen show the excerpt id and the first words of the excerpt.

issue: No 'looking ahead' note on SAS 151, The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud (approved by the ASB in August 2026). It supersedes AU-C 240 for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2028. AU-C 240 remains the 2026 testable standard, so nothing is wrong, but candidates who read the news may be confused.

source: AICPA ASB SAS 151 (2026); AICPA CPA Exam policy on new pronouncements
fix: Add one sentence: 'SAS 151 will replace AU-C 240 for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2028; it is not tested on the 2026 exam.'
